subject: Open Data Lab consortium — request for pilot trial top-up & extension
messages:
From: Dr. Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@opendatalab.edu>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Consortium pilot — request for trial top-up and short extension

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for getting us started on Redwood — the Open Data Lab consortium pilot across 6 universities has moved into the evaluation phase and we’re seeing promising results. We ran through our initial allocation faster than expected as a result of larger batch evaluations and longer context runs for the anonymization experiments.

Quick summary:
- Consortium: 6 partner universities; ~40 graduate researchers and 8 faculty leads.
- Current run rate: ~12M tokens / week during evaluation spikes.
- Primary use case: PII-aware text anonymization + prompt-based de-identification checks.
- Ask: additional compute credit equivalent to ~150,000 tokens and a 30-day extension on the trial window while we finish the evaluation.

Attached: proposal-opendatalab.pdf (pilot plan) and sample_prompts.csv (example prompt set + metrics we track).

We’re a nonprofit research consortium; if there’s any standard academic discount or research grant you can apply, that would help justify scaling to the production phase. We can sign a short MOU or confirm research-only usage terms.

Are you able to approve this request, or should we schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the numbers?

Best,

Lina Moreno
Director of Research — Open Data Lab
lina.moreno@opendatalab.edu
+1 415-555-0198

Short answers: we can usually approve research credits for nonprofit consortia, but I need to confirm the amount and the term with my credit approvals team. I’ve looped in Priyom (cc) to review the ask for 150k tokens and the requested 30-day extension.

Two quick clarifying items that will help speed approval:
1) What is the expected peak week token usage you want covered by the top-up? (you mentioned ~12M tokens/week during spikes)
2) Do the universities have an existing procurement/PO or a single PI who will sign the MOU? If you can confirm an approver and a billing contact, that helps us attach the voucher correctly.

If you prefer, we can approve a partial top-up while we finalize the MOU. Would you be available for a quick 20-minute call on Wednesday?

Thanks — I’ll aim to follow up by tomorrow after Priyom weighs in.

Best,

Team — forwarding Lina’s request for an academic nonprofit consortium pilot. Key context below; this will be a low-touch deal with potential for a Dedicated capacity discussion next year if they proceed to production.

Why approve?
- Nonprofit research consortium (6 universities) with strong path to grant funding and likely to scale if the eval goes well.
- They’ve hit their credit cap due to evaluation spikes; pilot produces good signals for anonymization product fit.

Request from client: 150k token top-up + 30-day extension.
My suggested offer: 150k token credit voucher, 14-day extension (we’re comfortable with limited-term extensions for pilots), and a research-only usage clause. Condition approval on a signed MOU (DocuSign link to follow) and a HubSpot deal update (HD-2026-1482).

Budget/impact: 150k tokens is small net revenue risk and precedent is aligned with previous academic waivers we’ve given (low conversion rate to revenue but high strategic value).

If we approve, I’ll issue a voucher (voucher-OPENDATA-2026.txt) and request the PI signs the DocuSign MOU. I’ll also update the HubSpot deal and tag this as research-promo.

Approve? If so I’ll draft the voucher and the DocuSign envelope and send back to Lina.

Thanks,
Marissa
